judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subsection ends by providing that amounts incurred "pursuant to this clause (e) shall be Lender Group Expenses" — a term that is nowhere defined in this bilateral agreement, so the cost-shifting consequence has no defined content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term is "Lender Expenses," which feeds the Obligations definition and the Section 2.3(b) waterfall; this stray label leaves a gap between the remedy and the recovery mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grants Lender a license to enter and occupy premises and to compromise conflicting Liens in its Permitted Discretion; broad but explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.4(d), 4.5 and the Collateral Access Agreement definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Set-off right with notice expressly waived but a duty to notify afterwards; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.6(b)'s bar on Cash Management Bank setoff and with Section 16.5's no-setoff rule against Borrowers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Right to hold balances as cash collateral; short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.6(d) and 3.6's cash collateral concept.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Uses inventory-finance boilerplate ("ship, reclaim, recover, store, finish ... advertise for sale") and takes a licence over labels, patents and trademarks, none of which fits a mortgage fund whose collateral is promissory notes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule 5.16 records no intellectual property at all, so the licence granted here has nothing to operate on — vestigial rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Public or private sale right measured by commercial reasonableness; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 9.1's Code-compliance lead-in and Section 9.1(k)'s notice rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Prescribes 15 days' written notice with a carve-out for perishable or recognized-market collateral, language again drawn from goods financing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to notice "as provided in Section 12," and Section 12 specially provides that enforcement notices are effective when deposited, which dovetails.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The credit-bid right is lettered "(h)" in the text although (h) has already been used for the cash-collateral right, so the subsection labelling in Section 9.1 breaks down.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.2 says numbering is for convenience only, which mitigates, but the mislabelling continues through the remaining clauses of Section 9.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits appointment of a receiver "without the requirement of prior notice or a hearing" to the maximum extent permitted by law; clear, and the lettering is again duplicated in the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the cumulative-remedies rule in Section 9.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A residual grant of "all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity," a pure catch-all after an enumerated list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.2 makes remedies expressly cumulative, which is the harmonising provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Again ends with "all such amounts shall be Lender Group Expenses," an undefined term, and it largely duplicates clause (e)'s servicing rights in different words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The overlap with clause (e) and with Section 4.8's revocation mechanism (which requires notice "in accordance with the terms of the Servicing Agreement") leaves two differently conditioned routes to the same remedy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard cumulative remedies and non-waiver clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforces Section 15.2; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Self-help rights on a payment failure, closing with the strong statement that Lender "need not inquire as to, or contest the validity of, any such expense, tax, or Lien" and that an official notice is conclusive evidence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (b) lets Lender set reserves against the Borrowing Base or the Maximum Revolver Amount with no Triggering Event condition, unlike the promise in Section 2.1(b), and it overlaps with Permitted Protests in Sections 6.7 and 6.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of waived notices; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the broader waivers in Section 2.13(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates all risk of loss to Borrowers subject to Lender's Code duty of reasonable care; the interaction of the two is stated but tight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.2's possession arrangements and Section 6.8's insurance covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad indemnity that expressly covers an Indemnified Person's own negligent acts (in capitals) while excluding gross negligence and willful misconduct; the express-negligence drafting is deliberate rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It survives termination and interlocks with Sections 14.1(b) (assignors keep Section 11.3 rights) and 16.11's separate indemnity, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deemed-receipt sentence is awkward ("deemed received on the earlier of the date of actual receipt or three Business Days after deposit") and the closing clause about facsimile effectiveness is garbled, leaving the effect of electronic notice unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.4 provides that any writing requirement is satisfied by a Record, which softens the formality here; the enforcement-notice carve-out matches Section 9.1(k).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An unambiguous New York choice of law for validity, construction and enforcement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.13(g)-(h) waives California anti-deficiency statutes and the Borrowers and collateral are Californian, so the governing-law clause and those waivers must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mandatory New York venue for the parties but an option for Lender to sue anywhere collateral is found — a one-sided asymmetry that could be construed against its drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.3 forbids construing ambiguity against either party, which cuts directly against that argument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard, conspicuous mutual jury waiver with an acknowledgment of counsel.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 13(b)'s venue provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits assignment of "all, or any ratable part of all" the Obligations in minimum $5,000,000 increments, then adds that the Assignee "need not be an Eligible Transferee" in a portfolio sale — an exception that largely undoes the eligibility requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the Eligible Transferee definition (which itself gives Administrative Borrower an approval right absent default), so the borrower's consent right is only as good as this carve-out allows.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States that an assignment "shall effect a novation between Borrowers and the Assignee," a legally loaded term used without elaboration, alongside survival of Section 16.8 obligations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.2 and the Section 11.3 carve-out preserved for assigning Lenders.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deems the Agreement amended "to the extent, but only to the extent, necessary" on receipt of an assignment; self-limiting and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It operates as an exception to Section 15.1's signed-writing requirement for amendments, a tension the drafters evidently intended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long participation clause with five specific protected voting matters and a set-off deeming rule; complex but carefully enumerated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves Lender as the sole counterparty for Sections 15.1 and 12, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits disclosure in connection with assignments, expressly subject to Section 16.8.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.8(f) contains the matching confidentiality exception; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Federal Reserve pledge clause with specific regulatory citations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overrides other provisions expressly ("Any other provision in this Agreement notwithstanding"), which is a clean priority rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Binds successors, voids borrower assignments "ab initio," and preserves Lender's assignment rights; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers accurately to Section 14.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires a signed writing from Lender and Administrative Borrower for any amendment or waiver, expressly excluding Bank Product Agreements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.1(c)'s deemed amendment and Sections 2.6(c)/6.9's schedule-amendment mechanics operate outside this rule, and Section 6.14 says notifications never amend the Agreement — a cluster that must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-waiver clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates Section 9.2's non-waiver language consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line effectiveness clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Closing Date definition and Section 16.6's counterparts rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: After disclaiming headings, it adds that "[u]nless the contrary is compelled by the context, everything contained in each Section applies equally to this entire Agreement" — a sweeping and unusual instruction whose effect on section-specific terms is genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it would spread section-specific rules (for example the Section 2.3(b) waterfall or Section 7's covenants) across the whole instrument, which cannot be reconciled with the Agreement's careful cross-referencing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Disclaims construction against either party and directs interpretation "according to the ordinary meaning of the words used so as to accomplish fairly the purposes and intentions of all parties" — two directives that can pull apart when the words and the purpose diverge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside Section 1.4's mandatory construction rules and Section 16.2's application rule, and it would be the first provision invoked in any contra proferentem argument about this lender-drafted form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare severability statement that says only that provisions are severable "for the purpose of determining the legal enforceability of any specific provision," without saying what happens to the rest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.16 makes any material provision being declared void an Event of Default, an awkward pairing with a severability regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The gross-up mechanism directs Borrowers to "comply with the penultimate sentence of this Section 16.5," a self-referential pointer that is hard to apply given the section's structure and the placement of the gross-up obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its no-setoff opening sentence complements Section 9.1(g)'s set-off right in Lender's favour; no other provision addresses withholding.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts and electronic execution clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.4's Record rule and Section 16.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Revival clause covering avoided transfers, extending to amounts Lender "elects to" repay on advice of counsel; the elective limb is broad but expressly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 2.13(i)'s reinstatement language and interacts with the Section 5.12 solvency representations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Confidentiality with seven enumerated exceptions and a two-year survival; the exceptions are specific rather than open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.1(e) cross-refers to this section, and Section 14.1(b) preserves it post-assignment; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure statutory notice with no operative obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Agreement bears on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration clause that says the Loan Documents "shall not be contradicted or qualified by any other agreement, oral or written, before the date hereof" — an unusual formulation that addresses prior agreements but not contemporaneous or later understandings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several operative terms depend on extrinsic documents delivered before closing (Borrower's Required Procedures, the written description underlying Permitted Reorganization, the Servicing Agreement), so an integration clause disclaiming prior writings is in tension with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Appoints Manager as irrevocable borrowing agent, then says the appointment lasts "unless and until" revoked — irrevocable and revocable in the same sentence — and adds a broad indemnity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with Section 2.13's joint liability and Section 6.12's separateness covenant, the latter of which pulls the other way by requiring the Borrowers to keep their affairs distinct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fill-in notice form with bracketed alternatives; the bracketed telephonic-confirmation language leaves the form partly optional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 2.12(c)'s Base Rate election mechanics, including the three-Business-Day lead time.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The certificate certifies compliance with "Sections 7.16, and 7.37" — there is no Section 7.37 — and paragraphs 2 and 5 restate the same representation twice in slightly different terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.3 requires this certificate to demonstrate compliance with Sections 7.16 and 7.17, so the exhibit's cross-reference is wrong, and its Schedule 3 restates the 0.9% leverage ceiling that cannot be met alongside the $50,000,000 facility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fill-in LIBOR election form with bracketed optional language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.12(b)'s deadline and the one-month Interest Period definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a specific account with a substitution mechanism; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The named account is at Greater Bay Bank, which sits against Section 2.6(a)'s Wells Fargo-only rule and Section 6.12(d)'s prohibition on other depository accounts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies Lender's account with a right to redesignate; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.3(a), 2.6(b) and 2.7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short items; item 2 is contingent ("Once a Permitted Reorganization is implemented, the Subordinated Liens securing Approved Debt") and does not identify the liens with any specificity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Liens clause (c) refers to liens "set forth on Schedule P-1" and to Approved Debt liens subject to a garbled subordination condition, and Section 2.1(b)(ii) refers to Schedule P-1 liens "specifically identified thereon" as having priority — none are.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lists two California licences with numbers and dates; factual and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.3 warrants that this schedule lists all licences required to conduct the business, which is a strong warranty resting on a very short list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short location entries; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.5, 6.9 and the Section 3.1(o) landlord waiver address.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States California for both Borrowers and "SUBSIDIARIES - NONE"; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Schedule 5.8 and the Subsidiary definition's exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single address; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.7(b), 6.9 and 12's notice address.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two identification numbers, partially redacted in the copy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.7(c) and 7.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States "None"; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.7(d) and 4.4(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrative capitalization description that mixes disclosure with characterisation, noting that redemption requests are granted "in the discretion of the Manager" and that 50 members' redemption requests were pending.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Those pending redemptions bear directly on Section 7.10's Restricted Payments regime, Section 8.9(x)'s default for failing capital obligations to members, and the Permitted Reorganization/Approved Debt structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two narrative litigation disclosures; factual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.10 excepts scheduled matters, so the disclosure functions as intended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States "None."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That makes the trademark and copyright machinery in Sections 4.4(c) and 9.1(i) inoperative, which is untidy but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short list of accounts with partially redacted numbers; the labels ("Lock Box - Cash Management Account," "Designated Account") are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: All the listed accounts are at Greater Bay Bank, which conflicts with Section 2.6(a)'s requirement that Wells Fargo be the only Cash Management Bank after 60 days and with Section 6.12(d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short factual entries cross-referring to Schedule 5.8.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Fremont Bank loan matches Schedule P-1 and Section 7.1(b), consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-column list of title insurers, garbled in places by the scan but identifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Approved Title Insurance Company definition and Section 5.21's non-affiliation warranty.
